chunks: What al-Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Indeed, sixty or seventy years may pass over a man while Allah has not accepted from him a single salat (prayer).” I said: “And how is that?” He said: “Because he washes what Allah has commanded to be wiped.”

key_terms.أَمَرَ: commanded, indicating the divine legal instruction
key_terms.سَبْعُونَ: seventy, further emphasizing the length of time
key_terms.سِتُّونَ: sixty, part of the expression indicating a very long period
key_terms.صَلَاةً: salat (prayer), the act of worship whose acceptance is being discussed
key_terms.قَبِلَ: accepted, meaning accepted by Allah as valid worship
key_terms.مَسْحِهِ: wiping it, the act Allah commanded in place of washing
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes, referring here to an incorrect act in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: How can incorrect wudu (ablution) affect the acceptance of salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the legal importance of performing wudu (ablution) exactly as commanded. It warns that altering an obligatory act of ritual purity—such as washing a limb that must be wiped—can invalidate worship and lead to the non-acceptance of salat (prayer) over many years. The report highlights precision in ritual practice as an essential part of obedience to Allah.
